in_english.long_meaning: Etienne is derived from the Greek name Stephnos, meaning steadfast, firm, and unwavering. In the New Testament, Stephanos ( Greek: Στεφανός) is the name of one of the first Christian martyrs, as recorded in Acts 6:5 and Acts 7:54-60. As a name, Etienne has been a popular choice in Christianity, symbolizing courage, resilience, and devotion. In Christian tradition, it is associated with strength, loyalty, and spiritual fortitude. The name Etienne has been borne by several Christian saints, including Saint Etienne de Bourbon, a 13th-century French saint known for his missionary work. In modern times, Etienne has become a popular choice for Christian parents seeking a name that reflects the values of faith, perseverance, and integrity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Etienne is popular in France and Belgium and is derived from the Latin name Stephanus. It was common among French-speaking Christians during the Middle Ages and remains a widely used name today.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, the name Etienne holds great spiritual significance as it refers to Stephen, the first Christian martyr. Stephen was a deacon in the early church and is remembered for his unwavering faith and steadfastness in the face of persecution. He is often depicted as wearing a crown or wreath, symbolizing his reward in heaven. This name is a reminder of the importance of faithfulness and resilience in the face of adversity, and of the ultimate reward that awaits those who remain true to their beliefs.
